newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER BACK IN CHASE AT PHOENIX OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER BACK IN CHASE AT PHOENIX OPEN.

text.p: After taking a week off to re-charge, Tiger Woods is back on the PGA Tour this week to join the chase for the $1.5 million Phoenix Open title at the Tournament Players Club starting Thursday.
With Woods out of the picture last week at the Bob Hope Chrysler Classic, John Cook fired a nine-under-par 63 on the final day of the 90-hole event to grab the $270,000 top prize.
Cook finished the five-round Hope tournament at 33-under 327 and was a stunning 19 under par on the final two days.

This week's event goes back to the standard 72 holes and four rounds and Cook and others will have to once again contend with Woods, who will be shooting for his fourth career win in only his 10th PGA tournament as a professional.
Woods, the 1996 Rookie of the Year, is one-for-one in 1997. He captured the season-opening Mercedes Championships, defeating Tom Lehman on first hole of playoff.
The playoff experience could come in very handy in Scottsdale, since the last two Phoenix Opens have been decided with extra holes.

Former Arizona State star and Scottsdale resident Phil Mickelson beat Justin Leonard on the third playoff hole to win in 1996 and Vijah Singh beat Billy Mayfair on the first sudden-death hole the year before. Briton Sandy Lyle also claimed this title in 1988 in a playoff.
Local knowledge seems to help and would work against Woods.
Since the tournament moved to Scottsdale in 1987, a local resident has won three times, with Calcavecchia taking honours in 1989 and 1992 before Mickelson.
The Phoenix Open has been contested since 1935, when Ky Laffoon's three-under 281 was good enough to win. The tournament record was established when Johnny Miller fired a 24-under 260 in 1975.
The Tournament Players Club of Scottsdale course is a par-71 and measures 6,992 yards.
